children: The dollar climbed to its highest level since July as Federal Reserve officials signaled that more rate hikes may be needed to fight inflation, according to Walter Bloomberg in a post on X.
rose 0.4% to $101.1 at the time of writing.

Markets were pricing a 53% chance of an October rate hike after last week's increase, the Fed's first in three years. ING said both the Fed and the European Central Bank could tighten again, although an October move appeared more likely from the Fed.

The elevated hike odds contrasted with expectations on Wall Street, where investors overwhelmingly believed the Fed would not raise rates at its Oct. 28 meeting, according to Jim Bianco of Bianco Research. The meeting comes one week before the U.S. midterm election, Bianco noted.

Fed hike odds had remained below 50% through mid-September, according to Bianco's chart. The probability stood at 26.6% on Sept. 10 and rose to 48.7% after the CPI reading on Sept. 11, before falling to 35.4% shortly before the Sept. 16 FOMC decision. The odds then jumped to 57.6% immediately after the Fed's rate hike and reached 59.8% on Sept. 22.
Bianco also pointed to a divergence between the Fed's policy rate and long-term Treasury yields. His post referred to the 10-year yield
rising during the Fed's rate-cutting cycle from 2024 through 2026, while the accompanying chart was titled “Fed Funds Target Rate US & US 30-Year Yield” and showed the 30-year yield.

Bianco said the period marked the first time in more than 50 years that a sustained rate-cutting cycle had coincided with rising long-term yields. He argued that the move represented a market message that the Fed had been too easy.

If markets continued pricing an October hike above 50% after next month's payrolls and CPI data, Bianco questioned whether a decision by the Fed not to hike could again prompt long-term yields to rise in response to what he called an "too easy" policy stance.

title: Dollar hits two-month high as Fed hike bets stay elevated
